Ask, don't assume; use professional interpreters (not family). Support the client's values & rituals. Kübler-Ross stages (not linear): denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance. Meet the client where they are. ⭐ The best therapeutic response usually names the client's feeling and invites them to say more — e.g., "You seem worried about going home. Tell me more about that." 🧪 Deep Dive: Lab Values & Fluid/Electrolyte Balance High-Yield Lab Values & Normal Ranges ＋ Deep Dive ★ High-yield

WBC 5,000–10,000/mm³ (high = infection/inflammation; low = immunosuppression → neutropenic precautions). Hgb: male 14–18, female 12–16 g/dL. Hct: male 42–52%, female 37–47% (≈3× the Hgb; high = dehydration). Platelets 150,000–400,000/mm³ — <50k = bleeding risk; <20k = spontaneous bleed → bleeding precautions.
Na⁺ 136–145 · K⁺ 3.5–5.0 · Ca²⁺ 9–10.5 mg/dL · Mg²⁺ 1.3–2.1 · Cl⁻ 98–106 · Phosphorus 3.0–4.5 · HCO₃⁻ 22–26. Pairs: K⁺ & Mg²⁺ track together; Ca²⁺ & phosphorus are inverse .

BUN 10–20 (↑ dehydration, kidney injury, high protein, GI bleed). Creatinine 0.6–1.2 = best kidney marker (diet/hydration don't sway it like BUN). Fasting glucose 70–110 · Albumin 3.5–5.0 (low → poor wound healing, edema) · Total bilirubin 0.1–1.0.

pH 7.35–7.45 · PaCO₂ 35–45 · PaO₂ 80–100 (<80 = hypoxemia) · HCO₃⁻ 22–26 · SaO₂ 95–100%. PT 11–12.5 / INR — warfarin therapeutic INR = 2–3 . aPTT 30–40 (heparin) — therapeutic = 1.5–2× control (≈46–70 sec). ⭐ Creatinine is the truest kidney marker; a rising creatinine is more reliable than BUN, which climbs with dehydration and high protein even when kidneys are fine. Electrolyte Imbalances — Signs & Treatment ＋ Deep Dive

Hypokalemia <3.5 Hyperkalemia >5.0 Weakness, ↓DTR, flat T-waves, U-waves, cramps, ileus, dysrhythmias Weakness, peaked T-waves, wide QRS, diarrhea/cramping, dysrhythmias → arrest Causes: diuretics, vomiting, diarrhea Causes: renal failure, K-sparing diuretics, crush injury Tx: oral/IV K (DILUTE, ≤10–20 mEq/hr, never push) Tx: Kayexalate, IV insulin+glucose, Ca gluconate, dialysis

Hypomagnesemia Hypermagnesemia ↑ excitability: +Trousseau/Chvostek, torsades; often with low K/low Ca ↓ everything: ↓DTR, ↓BP, ↓RR, lethargy (renal failure, Mg antacids/laxatives) Tx: IV magnesium sulfate Tx: stop Mg, IV calcium gluconate, dialysis Loss of DTRs on a Mg drip = toxicity. Low Mg or low K won't correct until the other is corrected. Low-calcium signs: C hvostek = C heek twitch when tapped; T rousseau = T ourniquet/BP-cuff causes hand spasm. ⭐ Peaked T-waves = hyperkalemia; flat T-waves + U-waves = hypokalemia; prolonged QT = hypocalcemia. Know the ECG-electrolyte trio. Fluids, Toni

Type Examples Action Isotonic 0.9% NaCl, LR, D5W* Stays in vessels — volume replacement/resuscitation Hypotonic 0.45% NaCl, 0.225% NaCl Moves INTO cells (rehydrates cells) Hypertonic 3% NaCl, D10W, D5½NS Pulls fluid OUT of cells into vessels *D5W is isotonic in the bag but acts hypotonic once dextrose is metabolized (free water → cells → risk of cerebral edema). Fluid bolus needs an 18-gauge or larger catheter.

Fluid Volume Deficit Fluid Volume Excess ↑HR, ↓BP, orthostatic, weak thready pulse, dry membranes, poor turgor, ↓urine ↑BP, bounding pulse, JVD, crackles, edema, dyspnea, ↑urine ↑Hct, ↑BUN, ↑urine specific gravity, weight LOSS ↓Hct (dilution), ↓specific gravity, weight GAIN (1 kg ≈ 1 L) Daily weight = best indicator of fluid status. Report >2 lb/day or >5 lb/week. Same scale, time, clothing. Infiltration: cool, swollen, pale, ↓flow → stop, remove, elevate, compress. Phlebitis: red, warm, tender, cordlike vein → stop, remove, warm compress. Air embolism: place LEFT lateral, head DOWN (left Tren

NCSBN Clinical Judgment (NCJMM): Recognize cues → Analyze cues → Prioritize hypotheses → Generate solutions → Take action → Evaluate outcomes. (Maps to ADPIE: Recognize=Assess, Analyze/Prioritize=Analysis, Generate=Planning, Take action=Implementation, Evaluate=Evaluation.) ISBAR hand-off: Introduction · Situation · Background · Assessment · Recommendation. Goals must be measurable + time-bound ("ambulate 50 ft by day 2," not "feel better").

Extinguisher classes: A = A sh (paper/wood) · B = B arrel (liquids/grease) · C = C ircuits (electrical); hospitals mostly ABC. Disaster triage flips ED logic: unsalvageable get a BLACK tag so resources go to the salvageable (opposite of "most critical first" in the ED). Body mechanics: bend knees/hips, back straight, wide base; #1 injury setup = twisting while lifting → pivot the whole body. ⭐ Conflict styles: Avoidance (manager ignores it / "does not intervene") is lose-lose and the classic wrong move. Collaboration is win-win. 👶 Deep Dive: Growth, Development & Advanced Assessment Growth & D

Infant = Trust vs Mistrust · Toddler = Autonomy vs Shame/Doubt · Preschool = Initiative vs Guilt · School-age = Industry vs Inferiority · Adolescent = Identity vs Role Confusion · Young adult = Intimacy vs Isolation · Middle adult = Generativity vs Stagnation · Older adult = Ego Integrity vs Despair.

Play: solitary (infant) → parallel (toddler) → associative/cooperative (preschool). Weight DOUBLES by 6 mo, TRIPLES by 12 mo. Posterior fontanel closes 6–8 wks, anterior 12–18 mo. Motor: 2 mo lifts head · 4 mo rolls front→back, no head lag · 6 mo sits with support · 8–9 mo sits unsupported/crawls · 12 mo pulls to stand, first steps, pincer grasp.

Expected: thinner/drier skin, ↓turgor, presbyopia, presbycusis (high-pitch loss), ↓taste/smell, ↓bladder capacity. NOT normal (investigate): confusion, increased salivation, skin thickening. ⭐ New confusion is NEVER "just aging." In an older adult, sudden confusion + incontinence = suspect a UTI/infection until proven otherwise. Advanced Physical Assessment ＋ Deep Dive
Standard: Inspect → Palpate → Percuss → Auscultate. Abdomen EXCEPTION: Inspect → Auscultate → Percuss → Palpate (palpating first alters bowel sounds); palpate tender areas LAST.

Auscultation "APE To Man": Aortic (2nd R), Pulmonic (2nd L), Erb's (3rd L), Tricuspid (4th L), Mitral/apex (5th L midclavicular). CN II = vision · III/IV/VI = eye movement · VII = facial movement + taste. Weber normal = equal both ears; Rinne normal = air > bone conduction. GCS = Eyes(4)+Verbal(5)+Motor(6) = 3–15; <8 = intubate . Unilateral blown/fixed pupil + ↓LOC = ↑ICP/herniation = emergency.

Sound Means Crackles (rales) Fluid in alveoli (HF, pneumonia) Wheezes Narrowed airways (asthma, COPD) Rhonchi Secretions in large airways (may clear with cough) Stridor Upper-airway obstruction — EMERGENCY Pleural friction rub Inflamed pleura (grating) ⭐ Levels of prevention: Primary = prevent (immunize/lifestyle) · Secondary = screen/detect early (BP screening, mammogram) · Tertiary = manage disease to limit complications (cardiac rehab, post-stroke PT). 🧠 Deep Dive: Psychosocial, Pharmacology & Comfort Psychosocial: Defense Mechanisms, Stress & Loss ＋ Deep Dive

Denial ("I don't have a problem") · Projection (blaming others for own feelings) · Rationalization (justifying with excuses) · Regression (adult reverting to childlike) · Displacement (yelling at the nurse instead of the boss) · Compensation (excelling in one area to offset another).

General Adaptation Syndrome: Alarm (fight-or-flight) → Resistance (adapts) → Exhaustion (depleted). Types of loss: Anticipatory (before) · Maturational (expected with development) · Situational (sudden/unexpected) · Complicated (prolonged, disabling → needs intervention). Culture/communication: always use professional interpreters — never family (especially children). ⭐ "I know how you feel — I lost my dad too" is inappropriate self-disclosure that shifts focus to the nurse. Reflecting the client's feeling and asking them to say more stays therapeutic. Pharmacology Deeper (PK, routes, errors,

First-pass effect: oral drugs hit the liver first → less reaches the blood. Half-life = time for 50% to clear (guides dosing frequency). Absorption speed: IV (immediate/complete, no take-backs) > IM/SubQ (fast if soluble + perfused) > Oral (slow/variable) > Topical/transdermal (slow, sustained).

Side effect (predictable/tolerable) · Adverse (harmful/unintended) · Toxicity (level too high) · Allergic/idiosyncratic. High-alert meds (independent double-check): insulin, heparin, opioids, K⁺. Med error: ASSESS the client FIRST → notify provider → complete incident report (never chart that a report was filed).

Desired ÷ Have × Quantity. Leading zero YES (0.5 mg); trailing zero NO (5 mg, not 5.0) — trailing zeros cause 10× overdoses. ⭐ After any med error the FIRST action is always to assess the client — paperwork (incident report) never comes before patient safety. Immunity, Endocrine Basics & Pain Deeper ＋ Deep Dive

Active = body MAKES antibodies, slow/long-lasting (vaccine, having the illness). Passive = antibodies GIVEN, immediate/temporary (maternal, immunoglobulin). Infection stages: Incubation → Prodromal (vague early sx) → Illness (full sx) → Convalescence (recovery).

Hypoglycemia Rule of 15: treat <70 with 15 g fast carb → wait 15 min → recheck; repeat if still low, then a complex carb + protein snack. WHO analgesic ladder: Step 1 non-opioid (acetaminophen/NSAID) → Step 2 weak opioid → Step 3 strong opioid; add adjuvants at any step. Acute vs chronic pain: acute = protective, <6 mo, ↑HR/↑BP/diaphoresis/grimacing; chronic = >6 mo, often NORMAL vitals + fatigue/depression.

Inflammatory (1–6 d, clot + cleanup) → Proliferative (3–24 d, granulation) → Maturation/Remodeling (day 21+, up to 1 yr). ⭐ Opioid #1 danger = respiratory depression; assess RR first and remember sedation precedes respiratory depression — a rising sedation level is the early warning to hold the dose. Big pooled NCLEX practice bank. 204 questions combined from four sources: the original ATI Fundamentals set (1–20), the ATI Interactive Quiz (21–104), and questions worked through in the exam-prep lecture recordings (105–204). Mix of multiple choice, SATA, matching, and dropdown items. Pick your a

entries.h: 1. Which task is appropriate for the RN to delegate to assistive personnel (AP)?
entries.t: a. Teaching a new diabetic about insulin b. Assisting a stable client to the bathroom c. Assessing a post-op wound for the first time d. Evaluating whether pain medication worked Check b. AP handle ADLs and ambulation for stable clients. Teaching, initial assessment, and evaluation require nursing judgment — RN only. Ethics

entries.h: 2. A competent client refuses a scheduled blood transfusion for religious reasons. The nurse's best action is to:
entries.t: a. Give it anyway since it's ordered b. Tell the client they could die without it and insist c. Support the decision, ensure it's informed, notify the provider, and document d. Ask the family to override the client Check c. Autonomy: a competent adult may refuse care. The nurse ensures the refusal is informed, notifies the provider, and documents. Giving it anyway = battery. Priority

entries.h: 3. Using the nursing process, which action does the nurse take FIRST for a newly admitted client?
entries.t: a. Plan measurable goals b. Collect a complete assessment c. Implement provider orders d. Evaluate outcomes Check b. ADPIE starts with Assessment — you can't plan, implement, or evaluate without data. Assess before acting. SATA

entries.h: 4. A client is on contact precautions for C. difficile. Which actions are correct? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Wash hands with soap and water b. Wear gown and gloves to enter the room c. Use alcohol-based hand rub only d. Dedicate equipment to the room e. Place the client in a negative-pressure room Check a, b, d. C. diff = contact precautions: gown/gloves, dedicated equipment, and soap & water (alcohol gel doesn't kill spores). Negative pressure is for airborne, not contact. Order

entries.h: 5. When removing PPE after client care, which item does the nurse remove FIRST?
entries.t: a. Mask b. Gown c. Gloves d. Goggles Check c. Doffing order removes the dirtiest first: gloves → goggles → gown → mask (mask comes off last, after leaving the room). Priority

entries.h: 6. A fire starts in a client's trash can. Applying RACE, the nurse's FIRST action is to:
entries.t: a. Pull the fire alarm b. Rescue clients in immediate danger c. Extinguish the fire d. Close all the doors Check b. RACE = Rescue first, then Alarm, Contain, Extinguish/Evacuate. People before property. SATA

entries.h: 7. Which clients require airborne precautions? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Active pulmonary tuberculosis b. Measles (rubeola) c. Influenza d. Varicella (chickenpox) e. Pertussis Check a, b, d. "My Chicken Hez TB" = Measles, Chickenpox/varicella, Herpes zoster (disseminated), TB → airborne + N95 + negative pressure. Influenza & pertussis are droplet . Priority

entries.h: 8. A client on a continuous tube feeding suddenly coughs and their SpO₂ drops to 86%. The nurse's FIRST action is to:
entries.t: a. Increase the feeding rate b. Stop the feeding and raise the head of bed c. Flush the tube with water d. Document the finding Check b. Signs of aspiration → stop the feed immediately and sit the client up to protect the airway, then suction/assess and notify the provider. Multiple choice

entries.h: 9. A client uses a cane for left-leg weakness. The nurse knows teaching is effective when the client holds the cane:
entries.t: a. In the left hand, moving it with the left leg b. In the right hand, advancing it with the left leg c. In whichever hand feels comfortable d. In the left hand, moving it with the right leg Check b. COAL — Cane Opposite Affected Leg. Hold in the strong (right) hand and advance the cane with the weak (left) leg together. Multiple choice

entries.h: 10. A pressure area on the sacrum has a shallow open ulcer with a red-pink moist wound bed and no slough. This is a:
entries.t: a. Stage 1 pressure injury b. Stage 2 pressure injury c. Stage 3 pressure injury d. Unstageable pressure injury Check b. Partial-thickness, shallow, pink-red moist bed with no slough = Stage 2. Stage 1 is intact skin; slough/eschar covering = unstageable. SATA

entries.h: 11. Which interventions help prevent complications of immobility? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Reposition at least every 2 hours b. Apply sequential compression devices c. Encourage incentive spirometer use d. Keep the client on strict bed rest indefinitely e. Provide range-of-motion exercises Check a, b, c, e. Prevent pressure injury (turn q2h), DVT (SCDs, ROM), and atelectasis (IS). Prolonged bed rest causes the complications — mobilize early. Multiple choice

entries.h: 12. Which client is the priority for the nurse to see FIRST?
entries.t: a. A client with a urine output of 20 mL over the last hour b. A client requesting a PRN laxative c. A client asking about discharge teaching d. A client whose dressing needs a routine change Check a. Output <30 mL/hr signals poor kidney perfusion/hypovolemia — an acute, changing physiologic problem. The others are stable/routine. Multiple choice

entries.h: 13. A postoperative client's ostomy stoma appears dusky and dark purple. The nurse should:
entries.t: a. Document it as an expected finding b. Apply a warm compress and recheck in 4 hours c. Notify the provider — this suggests ischemia d. Empty the pouch and reassess tomorrow Check c. A healthy stoma is pink/red and moist. Dark/dusky/purple = impaired perfusion (ischemia) — report promptly. Dropdown / Cloze

entries.h: 14. Complete the injection technique statements by choosing the best option:
entries.t: For a subcutaneous heparin injection, insert the needle at — select — 15° 45–90° exactly 10° and — select — do not aspirate or massage aspirate then massage firmly . The preferred, safest site for an IM injection in an adult is the — select — dorsogluteal deltoid for 3 mL ventrogluteal site. Check 45–90°; do not aspirate or massage; ventrogluteal. Heparin subcut is given at 45–90° with no aspiration/massage (↓bruising/hematoma). Ventrogluteal is the preferred IM site (away from major nerves/vessels); deltoid holds ≤1 mL. Multiple choice

entries.h: 15. A provider order reads "potassium chloride 20 mEq IV push now." The nurse should:
entries.t: a. Administer slowly over 2 minutes b. Hold the order and clarify — IV KCl is never pushed c. Give it with a rapid saline flush d. Dilute in 5 mL and push Check b. IV potassium is never given by push (fatal dysrhythmia) — always diluted on a pump. Question the unsafe order; "it was ordered" is not a defense. SATA

entries.h: 16. Which are correct steps in the "rights" of safe medication administration? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Verify the right client using two identifiers b. Leave the medication at the bedside if the client is busy c. Check the medication three times d. Document immediately after administration e. Recap the used needle to save it Check a, c, d. Two identifiers, three checks, and chart after (not before) giving. Never leave meds unattended or recap needles. Therapeutic communication

entries.h: 17. A client scheduled for surgery says, "I'm not sure I should go through with this." The best response is:
entries.t: a. "Don't worry, your surgeon is excellent." b. "Why would you cancel now?" c. "You sound unsure. Tell me more about what you're feeling." d. "I'll let the doctor know you're refusing." Check c. Names the feeling and invites the client to elaborate. "Why" questions sound accusatory, and false reassurance shuts down communication. Matching

entries.h: 18. Match each ethical principle to its definition:
entries.t: Autonomy — select — Do no harm Tell the truth Right to self-determination Fairness in care Nonmaleficence — select — Do no harm Tell the truth Right to self-determination Fairness in care Veracity — select — Do no harm Tell the truth Right to self-determination Fairness in care Justice — select — Do no harm Tell the truth Right to self-determination Fairness in care Check Autonomy = self-determination; Nonmaleficence = do no harm; Veracity = tell the truth; Justice = fairness. (Beneficence = do good; Fidelity = keep promises.) Multiple choice

entries.h: 19. A client stands up and reports dizziness; the nurse suspects orthostatic hypotension. This is confirmed by a systolic BP drop of at least:
entries.t: a. 5 mmHg b. 10 mmHg c. 20 mmHg d. 40 mmHg Check c. Orthostatic hypotension = systolic drop ≥20 mmHg (or diastolic ≥10) within 3 minutes of standing. Teach the client to change positions slowly and dangle first. Priority

entries.h: 20. A client receiving morphine via PCA has a rising sedation score. The nurse's priority is to:
entries.t: a. Encourage the family to press the button for them b. Assess respiratory rate and level of sedation before the next dose c. Increase the basal rate for better relief d. Document and continue as ordered Check b. Sedation precedes opioid-induced respiratory depression — assess RR and sedation first. Only the client presses a PCA button; never dose by proxy. Questions 21–104 · ATI Fundamentals Interactive Quiz Multiple choice

entries.h: 21. A nurse is developing a presentation about the Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM). Which step of the nursing process correlates with "analyze cues and prioritize hypotheses"?
entries.t: a. Assessment b. Analysis c. Planning d. Implementation Check b. Recognize Cues = Assessment. Analyze Cues + Prioritize Hypotheses = ANALYSIS. Generate Solutions = Planning. Take Action = Implementation. Evaluate Outcomes = Evaluation. Delegation

entries.h: 22. A nurse on a med-surg unit is making assignments. Which task should be delegated to the LPN/PN?
entries.t: a. Obtain vital signs for a client 2 hr post cardiac catheterization b. Administer a unit of packed red blood cells c. Instruct client on wound care prior to discharge d. Develop a care plan for a newly admitted pneumonia client Check a. Vital signs for a stable post-cath client = routine monitoring = appropriate for the PN. Blood transfusions require an RN, and teaching and care planning cannot be delegated. SATA

entries.h: 23. Which should be included in an orientation plan for newly licensed nurses? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Skill proficiency b. Assignment to a preceptor c. Budgetary principles d. Computerized charting e. Socialization into unit culture f. Facility policies and procedures Check a, b, d, e, f. Orientation = skills, preceptor, technology/charting, culture, and policies. Budgetary principles are a manager function, not new-nurse orientation. Multiple choice

entries.h: 24. A nurse manager does not intervene when conflict between team members escalates. Which conflict strategy is being used?
entries.t: a. Avoidance b. Smoothing c. Cooperating d. Negotiating Check a. Avoidance = no action taken even as conflict escalates ("does not intervene"). It is lose-lose. Smoothing = temporary peace; negotiating/compromising = both give something. SATA

entries.h: 25. Which are part of the 5 rights of delegation? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Right place b. Right supervision and evaluation c. Right direction and communication d. Right documentation e. Right circumstances Check b, c, e. The 5 rights: right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, right supervision/evaluation. "Place" and "documentation" are not among them. Multiple choice

entries.h: 26. After completing assessment of a newly admitted client, which action should the nurse take next?
entries.t: a. Orient the client to their room b. Develop a plan of care c. Review provider prescriptions d. Establish a care conference Check a. After assessment, orient the client — this reduces anxiety, establishes rapport, and improves safety. Care planning and reviewing prescriptions follow. Priority

entries.h: 27. A post-op client is not getting pain relief. What should the nurse do FIRST?
entries.t: a. Ask the provider for a different medication b. Assess the client's pain location, quality, and current status c. Administer the next scheduled dose earlier d. Document that pain management is ineffective Check b. Assessment always comes before intervention. Reassess the pain first — the location may have changed (a new problem) or the client may need repositioning before medication. SATA

entries.h: 28. Which actions decrease the risk of another fall for an oriented client in a nursing home? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Place belt restraint when sitting on bedside commode b. Keep bed in lowest position with all side rails up c. Make sure the call light is within reach d. Provide nonskid footwear e. Complete a fall-risk assessment Check c, d, e. Call light in reach, nonskid footwear, and a fall-risk assessment are appropriate. A restraint is inappropriate for an oriented client, and all four side rails up is itself a fall risk (climbing over). Priority

entries.h: 29. A client has a history of falls. Which is the nurse's PRIORITY action?
entries.t: a. Complete a fall-risk assessment b. Educate client and family about fall risks c. Eliminate safety hazards from the environment d. Make sure the client uses assistive aids Check a. Assessment first. The fall-risk assessment identifies the specific risk factors that direct every other intervention. Multiple choice

entries.h: 30. Which statement by a nurse about seizure care requires further instruction?
entries.t: a. "I will place the client on their side." b. "I will go to the nurses' station for assistance." c. "I will note the time that the seizure begins." d. "I will prepare to insert an airway." Check b. Never leave a seizing client. Stay and call for help using the call light. Side-lying, timing the seizure, and preparing an airway (for after) are all correct. Priority

entries.h: 31. A nurse observes smoke coming from under the staff lounge door. Which is the PRIORITY action?
entries.t: a. Extinguish the fire b. Activate the fire alarm c. Move clients who are nearby d. Close all open doors on the unit Check c. RACE: Rescue first — move clients in immediate danger. Then Alarm, Contain (close doors), and Extinguish last (only if safe). SATA

entries.h: 32. Which nursing responsibilities apply when caring for a client in restraints? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Explain the purpose of restraints to client and family b. Obtain written consent / provider order c. Assess skin integrity every 2 hours d. Tie restraints to the bed side rails for stability e. Offer ROM exercises f. Ensure 2 fingers fit under the restraint Check a, b, c, e, f. All are correct except tying to the side rails — tie to the bed FRAME (the part that moves with the controls). PRN restraint orders are never acceptable; ROM q2h prevents circulatory compromise. Multiple choice

entries.h: 33. A nurse is teaching home safety to a family with a 6-month-old infant. Which statement indicates understanding?
entries.t: a. "I will place my baby on their stomach to sleep to prevent SIDS." b. "I will put the baby in a rear-facing car seat until age 2." c. "I will use crib bumpers to protect the baby's head." d. "I can give the baby puffs or soft crackers as a snack." Check b. Rear-facing until age 2 is current guidance. Back-to-sleep (not stomach) prevents SIDS; crib bumpers are a suffocation risk; solid foods at 6 mo of this type are a choking risk. SATA

entries.h: 34. Which instructions should be included when teaching assistive personnel about handwashing? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Apply 3-5 mL liquid soap to dry hands b. Wash for at least 15 seconds c. Rinse with hot water d. Use a clean paper towel to turn off faucets e. Allow hands to air dry Check a, b, d. Correct soap amount on dry hands, 15 seconds minimum, and a paper towel to turn off the faucet. Use WARM water (hot damages skin), and dry with a paper towel (not air dry) before turning off the faucet. Multiple choice

entries.h: 35. On entering a room to change a surgical dressing, the nurse notes the client is coughing and sneezing. Which action should the nurse take?
entries.t: a. Keep the sterile field at least 6 ft from the bedside b. Instruct the client to refrain from coughing and sneezing c. Place a mask on the client to limit spread of microorganisms d. Keep facial tissues nearby for the client Check c. A mask on the client prevents respiratory droplets from contaminating the sterile field and open wound. You cannot reliably stop someone from coughing, and tissues don't protect the field. SATA

entries.h: 36. Which events contaminate a sterile field prepared for chest tube insertion? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Provider drops an instrument onto the near side of the field b. Nurse moistens a cotton ball with sterile saline and places it on the field c. Procedure delayed 1 hour due to an emergency call d. Nurse turns to speak to someone entering behind them e. Client's hand brushes against the outer edge of the field Check c, d, e. Prolonged air exposure, turning your back (loss of visual control), and touching the 1-inch border all contaminate the field. Dropping onto the center (not the border) stays sterile; adding sterile saline is acceptable. SATA

entries.h: 37. A nurse wearing sterile gloves may touch which objects without breaching sterile technique? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. A bottle containing sterile solution b. The edge of the sterile drape c. The inner wrapping of a sterile item on the field d. An irrigation syringe placed on the sterile field e. One gloved hand with the other gloved hand Check c, d, e. The inner wrapping, an item on the field, and sterile-to-sterile contact are all sterile. The solution bottle's outside is not sterile (only what is poured out), and the border/edge is always contaminated. Multiple choice

entries.h: 38. A nurse opens a sterile pack. Which flap should be unfolded first?
entries.t: a. The flap closest to the body b. The right side flap c. The left side flap d. The flap farthest from the body Check d. Open the farthest flap first (away from the body) to avoid reaching over the sterile field, then the sides, then the closest flap toward you last. SATA

entries.h: 39. A nurse is planning care for a client with suspected pertussis. Which interventions are appropriate? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Place the client in a negative-air-pressure room b. Wear a mask when providing care within 3 ft c. Place a surgical mask on the client for unavoidable transport d. Use sterile gloves when handling soiled linens e. Wear a gown when contamination from secretions is possible Check b, c, e. Pertussis = droplet precautions: mask within 3 ft, mask on the client during transport, gown if secretion exposure is likely. Negative pressure is for airborne only; clean (not sterile) gloves suffice for linens. Multiple choice

entries.h: 40. A nurse is sorting diseases by isolation type. Which assignment is correct?
entries.t: a. Tuberculosis = Droplet b. MRSA = Airborne c. Influenza = Contact d. Varicella = Airborne Check d. Varicella (chickenpox) = airborne (N95 + negative pressure), as is TB. MRSA = contact; influenza = droplet. Multiple choice

entries.h: 41. A nurse is caring for a client with C. difficile. Which hand hygiene method is required?
entries.t: a. Alcohol-based hand sanitizer only b. Soap and water c. Either alcohol gel or soap and water d. Antiseptic foam after gloves Check b. C. difficile requires soap and water — alcohol-based gel does not kill the spores. C. diff also requires contact precautions (gown + gloves). SATA

entries.h: 42. A client has hypovolemia due to vomiting and diarrhea. Which findings should the nurse expect? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Hypothermia b. Bradycardia c. Orthostatic hypotension d. Distended neck veins e. Decreased skin turgor Check a, c, e. Hypothermia (vasoconstriction), orthostatic hypotension, and decreased turgor are classic hypovolemia signs. Expect TACHYcardia (compensatory) and FLAT neck veins (distended = hypervolemia). SATA

entries.h: 43. Which findings indicate hypovolemia? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Increased Hct b. Increased blood pressure c. Decreased urine specific gravity d. Decreased urine output e. Increased sodium level Check a, d. Increased Hct (hemoconcentration) and decreased urine output (<30 mL/hr, kidneys conserving). BP is decreased and specific gravity is INCREASED (>1.030) in hypovolemia. Multiple choice

entries.h: 44. Which ECG finding does the nurse anticipate in a client with hyperkalemia (K+ = 5.8)?
entries.t: a. Prolonged QT interval b. Peaked T-waves c. Flat T-waves with U-waves d. Shortened PR interval Check b. Hyperkalemia = peaked (tall, tent-shaped) T-waves and risk of fatal arrhythmia. Flat T-waves + U-waves = hypokalemia; prolonged QT = hypocalcemia. Multiple choice

entries.h: 45. The nurse is assessing a client for Chvostek's sign. Which action should the nurse take?
entries.t: a. Apply a BP cuff and inflate above systolic for 3 minutes b. Listen to the carotid artery with a stethoscope c. Ask the client to lower their chin to their chest d. Tap lightly on the client's cheek over the facial nerve Check d. Chvostek's sign = tap the facial nerve at the cheek to elicit a facial twitch (hypocalcemia). Trousseau's sign uses the BP cuff; chin-to-chest is Brudzinski's (meningitis). SATA

entries.h: 46. Which findings are risk factors for hypocalcemia? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Bariatric surgery b. Diarrhea c. Thyroid cancer / thyroid surgery d. Diabetes mellitus e. Hyperlipidemia Check a, b, c. Bariatric surgery (malabsorption), diarrhea (GI losses), and thyroid/parathyroid surgery (parathyroid damage) all lower calcium. Diabetes and hyperlipidemia do not primarily cause hypocalcemia. Multiple choice

entries.h: 47. A nurse is preparing to administer potassium to a client with hypokalemia. Which route is contraindicated?
entries.t: a. Oral potassium with food b. IV potassium diluted in maintenance fluids c. IV push potassium d. Potassium-rich dietary sources Check c. Never IV push potassium — it causes fatal cardiac arrhythmia. Potassium must be diluted and infused on a pump, or given orally. SATA

entries.h: 48. A nurse is teaching an AP how to count respirations. Which instructions should be included? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Place the client in semi-Fowler's position b. Place one arm across the abdomen c. Observe respirations before counting d. Count for 30 seconds if the rate is irregular e. Inform the client you are measuring respirations Check a, b, c. Semi-Fowler's, arm across the abdomen, and observing first are correct. Count a FULL 60 seconds if irregular, and do NOT tell the client (they'll change their pattern). Priority

entries.h: 49. A client has a blood pressure of 140/94. What should the nurse do first?
entries.t: a. Administer antihypertensive medication as prescribed b. Ask the client if they are in pain c. Teach the client about a low-sodium diet d. Recheck the blood pressure in one hour Check b. Pain is the most common cause of an elevated BP in hospitalized clients. Assess the cause before treating — managing the pain may normalize the BP. Multiple choice

entries.h: 50. A client has an apical heart rate of 84 bpm and a radial rate of 68 bpm. What is the pulse deficit?
entries.t: a. 84 bpm b. 68 bpm c. 16 bpm d. 152 bpm Check c. Pulse deficit = apical − radial = 84 − 68 = 16 bpm. It indicates some cardiac contractions aren't strong enough to produce a palpable radial pulse. SATA

entries.h: 51. A client has a fever of 38.6°C. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Obtain cultures before administering antibiotics b. Restrict oral fluid intake c. Encourage rest d. Allow shivering to continue e. Provide oral hygiene Check a, c, e. Cultures before antibiotics, rest (lowers metabolic demand), and oral hygiene. INCREASE fluids (don't restrict) and PREVENT shivering (it raises heat production). Multiple choice

entries.h: 52. The nurse reviews a prescription for docusate 100 mg PO once daily. Which type of prescription is this?
entries.t: a. Single b. Stat c. Routine d. Now Check c. Routine = scheduled on an ongoing basis until discontinued. Single = one time; stat = immediately; now = within 90 minutes. Priority

entries.h: 53. The nurse administers the wrong medication. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
entries.t: a. Report the error to the risk manager b. Notify the provider c. Complete an incident report d. Check the client's vital signs Check d. Always assess the client first — check vital signs to determine if harm is occurring. Then notify the provider and complete the incident report. Client safety before paperwork. SATA

entries.h: 54. A nurse is caring for a client with evisceration. Which actions should the nurse take? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Cover with a sterile saline-soaked dressing b. Apply an abdominal binder tightly c. Apply direct pressure to the wound d. Position the client supine with knees bent e. Offer the client warm oral fluids Check a, d. Cover exposed viscera with a sterile saline dressing (keeps organs moist) and position supine with knees bent (reduces tension). No binders, no pressure, keep NPO (surgical emergency), and never push organs back in. Multiple choice

entries.h: 55. A client has a stage 3 pressure injury. Which description is accurate?
entries.t: a. Intact skin with non-blanchable redness b. Partial thickness with blister or shallow wound c. Full thickness with visible subcutaneous fat d. Bone, tendon, or muscle is exposed Check c. Stage 3 = full-thickness loss with visible fat but NO exposed bone/tendon/muscle. Stage 1 = intact/redness; Stage 2 = partial/blister; Stage 4 = bone/tendon/muscle exposed. Priority

entries.h: 56. A client returns from PACU after abdominal surgery. SpO2 is 91% on 2 L O2. Which action is priority?
entries.t: a. Increase O2 flow rate b. Position in semi-Fowler's and encourage deep breathing c. Notify the surgeon d. Administer a bronchodilator Check b. Position first — semi-Fowler's improves lung expansion and is first-line for a low post-op SpO2. Encourage deep breathing/coughing, then reassess before escalating. SATA

entries.h: 57. Which are adverse effects of opioid analgesics? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Urinary incontinence b. Diarrhea c. Respiratory depression d. Orthostatic hypotension e. Nausea Check c, d, e. Respiratory depression (most serious), orthostatic hypotension, and nausea. Opioids cause urinary RETENTION (not incontinence) and CONSTIPATION (not diarrhea). Priority

entries.h: 58. A client receiving morphine via PCA has a respiratory rate of 7/min and is difficult to arouse. Which action should the nurse take first?
entries.t: a. Stop the opioid and prepare to administer naloxone b. Reduce the PCA dose c. Notify the provider d. Apply oxygen and continue monitoring Check a. RR <8 + difficult to arouse = opioid-induced respiratory depression. Stop the opioid, give naloxone, stimulate, and support breathing. Sedation precedes respiratory depression. Multiple choice

entries.h: 59. A nurse notes thick, opaque, yellow-green, foul-smelling drainage from a surgical wound. How should the nurse interpret this?
entries.t: a. Serous — normal, seen early in healing b. Sanguineous — fresh bleeding c. Serosanguineous — normal post-op trend d. Purulent — infection; report immediately Check d. Thick, opaque, yellow/green, foul-smelling = purulent = infection; report and culture. Serous = clear/straw; sanguineous = bright red; serosanguineous = pink, blood-tinged (normal post-op). Multiple choice

entries.h: 60. A client's BMI is 27. How does the nurse classify this finding?
entries.t: a. Underweight b. Normal weight c. Overweight d. Obese Check c. BMI 25–29.9 = overweight. <18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; ≥30 obese. Multiple choice

entries.h: 61. Which lab finding indicates a catabolic state in a client with poor nutritional intake?
entries.t: a. Albumin 3.5 g/dL b. Negative nitrogen balance c. BMI 18.5 d. Prealbumin 15 mg/dL Check b. Negative nitrogen balance means protein breakdown exceeds synthesis — a catabolic/malnourished state. It is a more specific marker than a borderline albumin or prealbumin. Multiple choice

entries.h: 62. A client who had a partial gastrectomy reports dizziness, diarrhea, and tachycardia 20 minutes after eating. The nurse recognizes this as:
entries.t: a. GERD b. Paralytic ileus c. Dumping syndrome d. Peptic ulcer disease Check c. Early dumping syndrome occurs 15–30 min after eating from rapid gastric emptying and fluid shifts. Teach small meals, no liquids with meals, and lying down after eating. SATA

entries.h: 63. A client with celiac disease asks what foods are safe. Which responses are correct? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Graham crackers are safe b. Rice is safe c. Pasta is safe d. Corn tortillas are safe e. Barley soup is safe Check b, d. Rice and corn are gluten-free. Graham crackers and pasta (wheat) and barley all contain gluten. Strict lifelong avoidance is required. Multiple choice

entries.h: 64. A client is having a fecal occult blood test. Which instruction should the nurse include?
entries.t: a. Collect one sample from a single stool b. A blue result indicates a negative test c. Avoid urine contamination of the sample d. Red meat can be eaten up until the day of the test Check c. Avoid urine contamination. Collect 3 samples from 3 separate stools; blue = POSITIVE for blood; avoid red meat for several days before testing. Multiple choice

entries.h: 65. During a large-volume enema, the client reports cramping. What should the nurse do?
entries.t: a. Remove the rectal tube immediately b. Lower the enema bag to slow the flow c. Increase the height of the bag d. Tell the client to hold their breath Check b. Lower the bag to slow/stop the flow, reducing pressure and cramping. Raising it worsens cramping; removing the tube is premature. Priority

entries.h: 66. A client reports no bowel movement in 4 days with cramping and fullness; they normally have a daily BM. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
entries.t: a. Administer a PRN stool softener b. Assess the abdomen and ask about normal pattern, diet, fluid, and activity c. Prepare to administer a large-volume enema d. Notify the provider for a laxative order Check b. Assessment first — auscultate/palpate the abdomen and review baseline pattern and contributors (fluid, fiber, immobility, opioids). Enemas/stimulants are a last resort, not first-line. SATA

entries.h: 67. A nurse is teaching about preventing constipation. Which interventions should be included? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Increase dietary fiber gradually b. Limit fluid intake to prevent bloating c. Increase physical activity d. Respond promptly to the urge to defecate e. Use stimulant laxatives daily as a first-line measure Check a, c, d. Gradual fiber, activity (stimulates peristalsis), and responding to the urge. INCREASE fluids (2–3 L/day) and reserve stimulant laxatives as last-line (daily use causes dependence). Multiple choice

entries.h: 68. After completing the admission assessment of a client, which action should the nurse take next?
entries.t: a. Orient the client to the room and call light b. Develop a plan of care c. Review provider prescriptions d. Schedule a care conference Check a. Orient the client after assessment — reduces anxiety, builds rapport, and promotes safety. Planning and prescriptions follow. Priority

entries.h: 69. A client's SpO2 drops to 89% while resting in bed. Which is the nurse's priority intervention?
entries.t: a. Call the provider b. Administer oxygen via non-rebreather mask c. Elevate the head of the bed to Fowler's position d. Obtain an arterial blood gas Check c. Position first — elevating the HOB immediately improves lung expansion and oxygenation. Encourage deep breathing, then reassess before escalating O2 or calling the provider. Multiple choice

entries.h: 70. Which oxygen delivery device provides the most precise oxygen concentration?
entries.t: a. Nasal cannula b. Simple face mask c. Venturi mask d. Non-rebreather mask Check c. The Venturi mask delivers the most precise FiO2 — ideal for COPD clients who need controlled oxygen. The non-rebreather delivers the highest concentration but is least precise. Priority

entries.h: 71. A nurse is caring for a client with suspected tuberculosis. Which is the first action the nurse should take?
entries.t: a. Implement airborne isolation precautions b. Obtain a sputum culture c. Administer prescribed antibiotics d. Screen close contacts of the client Check a. Safety first — implement airborne precautions (N95 + negative-pressure room) to protect staff and other clients before any other step. SATA

entries.h: 72. An elderly client is admitted with acute confusion and urinary incontinence and no fever. Which nursing actions are appropriate? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Attribute the confusion to dementia without further investigation b. Obtain a urine culture and urinalysis c. Assess for other signs of infection d. Notify the provider of the change in mental status e. Implement infection control precautions as appropriate Check b, c, d, e. Acute confusion + incontinence in an older adult = UTI until proven otherwise, even without fever. Never attribute new confusion to dementia without investigating. Multiple choice

entries.h: 73. A client with herpes zoster has a unilateral vesicular rash following a dermatome. Which statement about transmission is accurate?
entries.t: a. The virus is spread by airborne transmission b. The virus is spread through direct contact with the vesicles c. The client is no longer contagious after the rash appears d. The virus cannot be transmitted to someone who had chickenpox Check b. Localized zoster spreads by direct contact with vesicle fluid; the client is contagious until all lesions crust over. (Disseminated zoster requires airborne + contact precautions.) Multiple choice

entries.h: 74. A nurse is caring for a client with COPD. What is the target SpO2 range?
entries.t: a. 95-100% b. ~88-92% c. Greater than 98% d. Less than 85% Check b. Target ~88–92% for COPD — too much O2 can suppress the hypoxic drive. Use a Venturi mask for precise delivery, but never withhold O2 from a hypoxic client. Multiple choice

entries.h: 75. A client receiving IV D5W develops confusion and cerebral edema. Which characteristic of this solution explains this?
entries.t: a. It is a hypertonic solution that pulls fluid from cells b. Once glucose is metabolized, it acts as a hypotonic solution c. It contains sodium that causes fluid retention d. It is an isotonic solution that expands vascular volume Check b. D5W is isotonic in the bag, but once glucose is metabolized the remaining free water acts hypotonic — water shifts into cells, causing swelling including cerebral edema. SATA

entries.h: 76. A peripheral IV site is cool, pale, and swollen with no blood return. Which actions should the nurse take? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Stop the infusion b. Apply a warm compress to the site c. Continue the infusion at a slower rate d. Remove the IV catheter e. Restart a new IV at a different site Check a, b, d, e. These are signs of infiltration. Stop the infusion, apply a warm compress (aids absorption), remove the IV, and restart elsewhere. Never keep infusing into an infiltrated site. Priority

entries.h: 77. Fifteen minutes into a blood transfusion, a client reports back pain, chills, and anxiety, with hypotension and dark urine. Which is the nurse's priority action?
entries.t: a. Notify the provider and blood bank b. Stop the transfusion and keep the vein open with NS c. Slow the transfusion rate and monitor VS d. Administer diphenhydramine IV Check b. These are signs of an acute hemolytic reaction — the most dangerous. STOP the transfusion immediately and keep the vein open with NS; then notify provider/blood bank. Never just slow it. SATA

entries.h: 78. Which actions are required before starting a blood transfusion? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Verify the blood product at the bedside with another nurse b. Prime the tubing with D5W c. Obtain informed consent from the client d. Use an 18-gauge or larger IV catheter e. Begin the infusion at a rapid rate for the first 15 minutes Check a, c, d. Two-nurse verification, informed consent, and an 18-gauge (or larger) catheter. Prime with NS only (D5W hemolyzes RBCs), and begin SLOWLY for the first 15 minutes while watching for a reaction. Multiple choice

entries.h: 79. A client on IV fluids suddenly develops shortness of breath, sharp chest pain, and hypotension; the nurse suspects an air embolism. Which position is correct?
entries.t: a. High Fowler's with feet elevated b. Left lateral decubitus with head down (Trendelenburg) c. Supine with legs elevated d. Right lateral decubitus with HOB elevated 30° Check b. Left lateral with head down (left Trendelenburg) traps the air in the right ventricle, away from the pulmonary artery. Then give O2, call the provider, and monitor VS. Multiple choice

entries.h: 80. While inserting a Foley in a female client, after 3 inches there is no urine return; the nurse suspects the catheter is in the vagina. Which is correct?
entries.t: a. Remove the catheter and start over with the same catheter b. Leave the catheter as a landmark and insert a new sterile catheter into the urethra c. Advance the catheter further d. Pull the catheter back 1 inch and redirect Check b. Leave the misplaced catheter as a landmark for the vaginal opening, then use a NEW sterile catheter for the urethra. Reusing the same catheter contaminates the field. SATA

entries.h: 81. Discharge teaching for a client with a long-term indwelling catheter should include which instructions? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Keep the drainage bag below the level of the bladder at all times b. Disconnect the catheter from the tubing to empty the bag c. Clean the perineal area and catheter with soap and water daily d. Drink at least 2-3 L of fluid per day unless restricted e. Use a separate container to empty each client's drainage bag Check a, c, d. Bag below the bladder (prevents backflow), daily perineal/catheter care, and increased fluids. Never disconnect the closed system (infection risk); the separate-container rule is a facility practice, not self-care. Priority

entries.h: 82. An elderly client is admitted with new-onset confusion, agitation, and urinary incontinence; temperature 37.2°C. Which is the nurse's priority action?
entries.t: a. Attribute the confusion to dementia b. Administer PRN lorazepam for agitation c. Obtain a urine specimen for urinalysis and culture d. Apply a urinary catheter for incontinence Check c. Older adults show atypical infection signs — new confusion/incontinence without fever. UTI is most common; obtain a specimen for UA/culture before antibiotics. Multiple choice

entries.h: 83. When caring for a client with an indwelling urinary catheter, which nursing action is correct?
entries.t: a. Raise the drainage bag to bladder level when repositioning b. Irrigate the catheter every 8 hours to maintain patency c. Secure the catheter to the client's thigh to prevent tension d. Disconnect the tubing briefly to obtain a urine specimen Check c. Secure the catheter to the thigh (female) or lower abdomen (male) to prevent tension/trauma. Never raise the bag above the bladder, irrigate only with orders, and sample from the port (never open the closed system). Priority

entries.h: 84. A client informed about surgery is about to sign the consent form but says, "I'm not sure I understand what they told me." Which is the nurse's priority action?
entries.t: a. Explain the procedure and its risks in detail b. Have the client sign the form and note their concern c. Notify the provider that the client has questions before proceeding d. Tell the client the surgeon already explained everything Check c. The provider (not the nurse) explains the procedure/risks. If the client has questions, STOP and notify the provider — never pressure them to sign. Multiple choice

entries.h: 85. A client with terminal cancer states they do not want to be resuscitated, but there is no written DNR order. Which action should the nurse take?
entries.t: a. Honor the wish and document the verbal request b. Notify the provider to obtain a written DNR order c. Initiate CPR since there is no written order d. Contact the family to verify the client's wishes Check b. A DNR must be a written provider order to be valid. Notify the provider to get it written; until then, full resuscitation is required by law. Multiple choice

entries.h: 86. A nurse discloses a client's HIV status to a family member without permission. This is an example of which violation?
entries.t: a. Negligence b. Malpractice c. HIPAA violation d. Informed consent violation Check c. Sharing protected health information (especially HIV status) with unauthorized people is a HIPAA violation. It requires the client's explicit written consent. Priority

entries.h: 87. A client tells the nurse they want to leave against medical advice (AMA). The nurse should take which action first?
entries.t: a. Physically prevent the client from leaving b. Notify the provider of the client's decision c. Have the client sign the AMA form immediately d. Tell the client they cannot leave without the doctor's permission Check b. Notify the provider first so the client can be informed of the risks, then offer (not force) the AMA form. A competent adult may leave; physically restraining them is false imprisonment. Multiple choice

entries.h: 88. A nurse questions a prescription that seems potentially harmful. Which ethical principle is the nurse demonstrating?
entries.t: a. Autonomy b. Beneficence c. Nonmaleficence d. Fidelity Check c. Nonmaleficence = do no harm. Questioning a potentially harmful order demonstrates this. Autonomy = the client's right to decide; beneficence = do good; fidelity = keep promises. Multiple choice

entries.h: 89. A nurse made a documentation error in the medical record. Which action should the nurse take?
entries.t: a. Use correction fluid and write over it b. Completely cross out the error so it is illegible c. Draw a single line through the error, write "error" and initials, and document correctly d. Erase the entry and rewrite it Check c. Single line through the error, write "error" + initials + date, then the correct entry. Never white-out, erase, or obscure — the record is a legal document and must stay readable. Therapeutic communication

entries.h: 90. A client scheduled for surgery says, "I'm really nervous about the anesthesia." Which therapeutic response is most appropriate?
entries.t: a. "There is nothing to be worried about. It's very safe." b. "I know exactly how you feel. I was nervous before my own surgery." c. "Tell me more about what concerns you about the anesthesia." d. "The anesthesiologist is very experienced. You'll be fine." Check c. An open-ended invitation to explore feelings is best. Options a and d are false reassurance; b is inappropriate self-disclosure that shifts focus to the nurse. Multiple choice

entries.h: 91. A nurse is calling a provider to report a change in a client's condition. Which framework should the nurse use?
entries.t: a. ADPIE b. RACE c. SBAR d. PASS Check c. SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) is the standardized format for reporting to providers. ADPIE = nursing process; RACE = fire; PASS = extinguisher. SATA

entries.h: 92. Which are examples of non-therapeutic communication? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. "Why didn't you tell your doctor about your symptoms sooner?" b. "It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed." c. "Don't worry, the procedure will be over quickly." d. "What has been the most difficult part of this for you?" e. "I know how you feel — I lost my father too." Check a, c, e. "Why" questions are judgmental, "don't worry" is false reassurance, and "I know how you feel" is inappropriate self-disclosure. Reflecting feelings (b) and open-ended questions (d) are therapeutic. Multiple choice

entries.h: 93. Which is an example of correct objective documentation?
entries.t: a. Client seems anxious today b. Client ambulated 30 feet in hallway with steady gait using walker c. Client had a good day overall d. Wound looks OK Check b. Objective = measurable/observable. "Ambulated 30 feet with steady gait" is factual. "Seems," "good day," and "OK" are subjective/vague — avoid them. Multiple choice

entries.h: 94. A nurse is repositioning an immobile client. Which action demonstrates correct body mechanics?
entries.t: a. Bending at the waist to lower the client b. Twisting the torso while moving the client c. Keeping the feet together during the lift d. Bending at the knees and keeping the back straight Check d. Bend at the knees/hips, keep the back straight, and use a wide base. Bending at the waist and twisting cause back injury; feet together is an unstable base. Multiple choice

entries.h: 95. A nurse is providing oral care to an unconscious client. Which action should the nurse take first?
entries.t: a. Position the client in semi-Fowler's b. Position the client in a lateral (side-lying) position c. Insert a bite block before beginning d. Apply oral swabs dipped in lemon glycerin Check b. Place an unconscious client in the lateral position for oral care to prevent aspiration, with suction available. Semi-Fowler's risks aspiration; lemon-glycerin swabs dry the mucosa. Priority

entries.h: 96. A client is on bed rest for 5 days. Which intervention is the highest priority to prevent complications of immobility?
entries.t: a. Encourage a high-fiber diet b. Reposition the client every 2 hours c. Apply sequential compression devices d. Initiate range-of-motion exercises twice daily Check b. Repositioning q2h is highest priority — it prevents pressure injuries (the most immediate serious risk) and improves circulation and respiratory status. All options matter, but this addresses the most immediate risk. Multiple choice

entries.h: 97. Which position should the nurse use for a client experiencing an air embolism during IV therapy?
entries.t: a. High Fowler's b. Prone with HOB down c. Left lateral decubitus with head down (Trendelenburg) d. Supine with legs elevated Check c. Left lateral with head down (left Trendelenburg) traps the air bubble in the right ventricle, preventing it from entering the pulmonary artery. Call for help, give O2, monitor VS. Multiple choice

entries.h: 98. Using the "CARD GP" mnemonic for complications of immobility, which complication is associated with the GI system?
entries.t: a. DVT and pulmonary embolism b. Atelectasis c. Constipation and paralytic ileus d. Pressure injuries Check c. CARD GP: Cardiovascular (DVT), Atelectasis/respiratory, Renal/GU, Depression, GI (constipation/ileus), Pressure injuries. GI prevention: fluids/fiber, stool softeners, early ambulation. Multiple choice

entries.h: 99. Preoperative teaching for a client scheduled for abdominal surgery should include which information?
entries.t: a. "You may eat a light breakfast on the morning of surgery." b. "We will keep you in bed until the morning after surgery." c. "When you cough after surgery, hold a pillow against your incision." d. "Do not use the incentive spirometer more than once per day." Check c. Splinting the incision with a pillow when coughing reduces pain and supports the wound. Clients are NPO (no breakfast), early ambulation is encouraged, and the incentive spirometer is used ~10x/hr while awake. Multiple choice

entries.h: 100. In which order should assessment techniques be performed for the ABDOMEN?
entries.t: a. Inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation b. Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation c. Auscultation, inspection, percussion, palpation d. Percussion, auscultation, inspection, palpation Check b. The abdomen is the exception: Inspect → Auscultate → Percuss → Palpate. Palpation is last because pressing on the abdomen can alter bowel sounds. Multiple choice

entries.h: 101. A nurse auscultates crackling, moist sounds in the lower lobes bilaterally. How should this be documented?
entries.t: a. Wheezes noted in bilateral lower lobes b. Rhonchi noted in bilateral lower lobes c. Crackles noted in bilateral lower lobes d. Pleural friction rub noted in bilateral lower lobes Check c. Crackles (rales) = crackling, moist sounds from fluid in the alveoli (pulmonary edema, pneumonia). Wheezes = high-pitched (bronchoconstriction); rhonchi = low-pitched secretions in large airways. Multiple choice

entries.h: 102. Recommending annual blood pressure screenings is an example of which level of prevention?
entries.t: a. Primary prevention b. Secondary prevention c. Tertiary prevention d. Quaternary prevention Check b. Screening to detect disease early = secondary prevention. Primary = prevent disease (immunizations, lifestyle); tertiary = manage existing disease to prevent complications. Multiple choice

entries.h: 103. According to Erikson, which behavior demonstrates age-appropriate development for a 2-year-old?
entries.t: a. Developing a sense of industry through school projects b. Exploring career identity through peer relationships c. Asserting independence by insisting on doing tasks alone d. Building trust through consistent caregiver response Check c. Autonomy vs Shame/Doubt (ages 1–3): the toddler asserts independence ("I do it myself"). Industry = school age; Identity = adolescent; Trust = infant. Multiple choice

entries.h: 104. A client who signed a surgical consent states, just before going to the OR, that they have changed their mind. What should the nurse do?
entries.t: a. Proceed since the consent was already signed b. Stop the process and notify the provider immediately c. Have the client sign a new consent reversing the first d. Tell the client it is too late to change their mind Check b. A client can withdraw consent at any time, even after signing. Stop and notify the provider — the nurse never pressures the client to continue. Questions 105–204 · from the exam-prep lecture recordings Multiple choice

entries.h: 105. A nurse is caring for a client with fluid volume excess who is short of breath and edematous. The client is anxious and requests more information about the treatment plan. How should the nurse advocate for the client's rights?
entries.t: a. Administer diuretics without discussing the plan to avoid stressing the client b. Encourage the client to trust the team and not ask too many questions c. Tell the client the plan is standard and needs no further explanation d. Explain the treatment plan in detail and ensure the client understands the rationale Check d. A client requesting information has a right to it; the nurse must advocate for understanding. Options a-c all shut down communication. NCLEX favors "explain and ensure understanding." Multiple choice

entries.h: 106. A community health nurse teaches older adults about preventing electrolyte imbalances. Which teaching point is most effective?
entries.t: a. Drink water only when you feel thirsty b. Limit fluid intake to 1,000 mL/day c. Maintain adequate hydration, especially during hot weather d. Replace sports drinks with water for all hydration needs Check c. Older adults have a blunted thirst response, so "drink only when thirsty" is unsafe. Watch for absolutes and unjustified fluid restriction (<2-3 L/day needs a reason). Multiple choice

entries.h: 107. A nurse documents intake/output over a 12-hour shift: 1 cup coffee, 2 cups water, 3 tbsp ice, emesis 120 mL. IV intake equals urine output. What is the fluid balance?
entries.t: a. 645 mL b. 622.5 mL c. -745.5 mL d. -120 mL Check b. Ice chips count as half volume (3 tbsp = 45 mL → 22.5 mL). Because IV intake equals urine output they cancel out. Intake minus output = 622.5 mL. Multiple choice

entries.h: 108. A client had major abdominal surgery with significant blood loss; BP 90/50, HR 120, cool clammy skin. Which IV fluid is most appropriate for immediate volume resuscitation?
entries.t: a. 0.45% NS (half NS) b. D5W c. 0.9% NS d. D5 half NS Check c. An isotonic fluid stays in the intravascular space to support a hypotensive, hypovolemic client. Hypotonic and dextrose fluids leave the bloodstream too quickly. Multiple choice

entries.h: 109. A client with severe pancreatitis develops carpopedal spasms the next day. Which lab finding is the nurse most likely to assess?
entries.t: a. Hypocalcemia b. Hyperkalemia c. Hypoalbuminemia d. Hypermagnesemia Check a. Calcium migrates to areas of inflammation in severe pancreatitis, lowering serum calcium. Muscle spasms/tingling (Trousseau's, Chvostek's) point to low calcium (or low magnesium). SATA

entries.h: 110. After running a marathon, a client has diaphoresis and generalized weakness; Na 129, K 3.6. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Administer 0.9% sodium chloride IV b. Initiate seizure precautions c. Provide high-sodium foods d. Administer potassium chloride IV e. Administer 0.45% sodium chloride IV f. Closely monitor I&O Check a, b, c, f. Treat the abnormal (low sodium) and don't "fix" the normal potassium. Low sodium risks seizures, so seizure precautions and I&O monitoring are appropriate. 0.45% would worsen hyponatremia. SATA

entries.h: 111. A nurse reinforces diet teaching after a sleeve gastrectomy. Which instructions reduce postoperative complications? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Drink fluids between meals b. Eat high-protein foods c. Refrain from drinking liquid calories d. Increase intake of concentrated sweets e. Chew food thoroughly before swallowing f. Do not exceed a meal size of 2 cups g. Eat foods high in nutrients Check a, b, c, e, g. Separating fluids from meals prevents overdistension/dumping. Avoid concentrated sweets. Meal size should not exceed 1 cup (not 2), so f is a misconception. Priority

entries.h: 112. A nurse assesses a client 36 hours after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Which finding is most concerning for an anastomotic leak?
entries.t: a. Temperature 100.4°F (38°C) b. Heart rate 118 c. Pain 6/10 at incision d. Decreased bowel sounds Check b. Tachycardia (HR >100) is often the earliest sign of an anastomotic leak, appearing before fever or abdominal pain. The others are expected post-op. SATA

entries.h: 113. A client is post-op day 3 after bariatric surgery; the nurse suspects dumping syndrome. Which findings support this? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Abdominal cramping b. Diarrhea c. Bradycardia d. Dizziness after meals e. Severe constipation Check a, b, d. Rapid fluid shift into the gut causes vasomotor symptoms-cramping, diarrhea, dizziness/tachycardia. Look for opposites: bradycardia and constipation rule out. Priority

entries.h: 114. Which psychosocial factor is most important to assess before a client undergoes bariatric surgery?
entries.t: a. Financial stability b. Support system c. Employment status d. Housing situation Check b. The surgery demands permanent lifestyle change; a strong support system provides the emotional/practical help needed for long-term success. Multiple choice

entries.h: 115. A client is 1 day post total hip replacement. Which intervention is most effective in preventing VTE?
entries.t: a. Elevate the affected extremity every 4 hours b. Encourage adequate hydration c. Implement early ambulation d. Apply elastic stockings while in bed Check c. Early ambulation is the gold standard-it directly addresses venous stasis (Virchow's triad) by promoting venous return. Stockings are passive. Priority

entries.h: 116. A client has decreased urine output in the immediate post-op period. What should the nurse do first?
entries.t: a. Perform a bladder scan b. Insert a urinary catheter c. Encourage oral fluid intake d. Obtain serum BUN and creatinine Check a. Anesthesia can cause retention. A quick, noninvasive bladder scan tells you whether urine is being made but not released; start with least invasive. If the action changes based on the assessment, assess first. Priority

entries.h: 117. During general anesthesia a client suddenly develops HR 167, BP 92/57, temp 40°C (104°F). Which action should the nurse prioritize?
entries.t: a. Administer dantrolene sodium immediately b. Apply cooling blankets and ice packs c. Administer acetaminophen IV d. Notify the client's family Check a. Dantrolene is the only drug that treats the underlying muscle-metabolism crisis of malignant hyperthermia. Cooling is only supportive; acetaminophen won't touch heat from muscle breakdown. Multiple choice

entries.h: 118. A terminally ill, competent client whose family insists on aggressive treatment says, "I just want to be done with all of this and be comfortable." What is the nurse's best response?
entries.t: a. I understand, but you have to convince your family b. Let's talk to the provider about what you want your care to be c. You should listen to your family, since they care about you d. I'll inform your family that you want to stop all treatments Check b. A competent client is the decision maker. The nurse supports the client speaking with the provider, without acting as intermediary or applying family pressure. SATA

entries.h: 119. While completing a medication reconciliation, the family asks why they keep answering the same questions. The nurse explains it is necessary because... (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. A med rec is completed whenever a client is admitted b. An up-to-date med rec reduces potential errors in treatment c. Employees can only see their own charting d. A thorough med rec reduces potential errors in charting e. An additional set of eyes to assess the med rec is helpful Check a, b, d, e. Med rec is done on admission/transfer/discharge, needs two sources, and reduces treatment/charting errors. Option c is false. Multiple choice

entries.h: 120. A client with diabetes cries, "I cannot stand the thought of giving myself these shots for the rest of my life." What is the best response?
entries.t: a. If you don't give the insulin, you'll be at greater risk for complications b. We can teach a family member to give the shot c. I can arrange a home health nurse to give the shots daily d. What is it about giving yourself the insulin shots that bothers you? Check d. Psychosocial answers explore the client's feelings. Identifying the specific fear (e.g., needle size) lets the nurse address it. Option a is threatening; b and c are unrealistic long-term. SATA

entries.h: 121. A nurse teaches a client with a history of hyperkalemia which foods to avoid. Which foods should be included? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Avocado b. Banana c. Lettuce d. Potato e. Apple f. Orange Check a, b, d, f. Avocado, banana, potato, and orange are high in potassium. Lettuce (mostly fiber/water) and apples are relatively low. Multiple choice

entries.h: 122. An older adult with CKD has a new serum creatinine of 2.3 (normal 0.6-1.2). What action should the nurse take?
entries.t: a. Encourage increased fluid intake b. Notify the healthcare provider immediately c. Review the client's medications for nephrotoxic drugs d. Reassure the client this is normal aging Check c. It's a chronic, non-emergent elevation from weak kidneys. Reviewing for nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) is appropriate; extra fluids won't help and could cause overload. Creatinine does not rise significantly with normal aging. Multiple choice

entries.h: 123. A nurse cares for a client in respiratory alkalosis. Which intervention is most appropriate?
entries.t: a. Administer sodium bicarbonate b. Encourage slow, deep breathing c. Provide supplemental oxygen d. Administer a diuretic Check b. Hyperventilation blows off CO2 (acid), raising pH. Slowing breathing lets CO2 rise back to normal-treating the cause. Bicarb would worsen alkalosis. Multiple choice

entries.h: 124. ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 42, HCO3 18. Which imbalance should the nurse identify?
entries.t: a. Respiratory acidosis with partial compensation b. Respiratory acidosis with no compensation c. Metabolic acidosis with partial compensation d. Metabolic acidosis with no compensation Check d. Low pH = acidosis; normal CO2 rules out respiratory cause; low bicarb = metabolic. Normal CO2 means compensation hasn't begun. Multiple choice

entries.h: 125. A client with type 1 diabetes has nausea/vomiting, high glucose, rapid deep breathing with fruity breath, hot dry skin. Which ABG best reflects this?
entries.t: a. pH 7.24, PaCO2 55, HCO3 22 b. pH 7.33, PaCO2 44, HCO3 17 c. pH 7.1, PaCO2 75, HCO3 35 d. pH 7.44, PaCO2 66, HCO3 58 Check b. DKA causes metabolic acidosis-low pH with low bicarb; CO2 may fall as respiratory compensation (Kussmaul). Multiple choice

entries.h: 126. ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 61, HCO3 30. Which condition is the client most likely experiencing?
entries.t: a. Diabetic ketoacidosis b. COPD exacerbation c. Panic attack with hyperventilation d. Intractable vomiting for 5 days Check b. Respiratory acidosis with partial compensation (low pH, high CO2, elevated bicarb) fits chronic CO2 retention in COPD. Multiple choice

entries.h: 127. A client with intractable vomiting for 3 days has ABG pH 7.52, PaCO2 48, HCO3 36. Which imbalance best explains this?
entries.t: a. Metabolic alkalosis with partial compensation b. Metabolic alkalosis with full compensation c. Respiratory alkalosis with full compensation d. Respiratory alkalosis with no compensation Check a. Loss of gastric acid → high pH, high bicarb = metabolic alkalosis. pH is still abnormal, so compensation is only partial. Priority

entries.h: 128. A 29-year-old presents with sudden SOB, chest tightness, dizziness that began before a nursing exam; pH 7.5, PaCO2 28, HCO3 24, RR 34, SpO2 99% RA, HR 112, alert/anxious/trembling. Which action should the nurse prioritize?
entries.t: a. Administer a PRN benzodiazepine b. Prepare for repeat ABG testing c. Encourage the client to breathe slowly into a paper bag d. Administer sublingual nitroglycerin Check c. This is a panic attack causing respiratory alkalosis; rebreathing CO2 with a paper bag restores acid balance-least invasive first. Priority

entries.h: 129. A post-op client on IV morphine PCA reports pain 8/10, is difficult to arouse, RR 8. Which action should the nurse take first?
entries.t: a. Increase the PCA dose b. Administer naloxone as prescribed c. Encourage more frequent PCA use d. Reassess pain in 30 minutes Check b. RR 8 with decreased LOC is opioid-induced respiratory depression; naloxone reverses it. Breathing takes precedence over pain; monitor for rebound since opioids outlast naloxone. SATA

entries.h: 130. A hospitalized client with moderate pain says, "I want to try something other than medications." Which nursing interventions support pain management? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Begin a PCA medication b. Lead the client through guided imagery c. Instruct the client in relaxation breathing techniques d. Offer ibuprofen 600 mg PO e. Apply ice to areas with impaired circulation f. Distract the client with music or television Check b, c, f. The client wants non-drug options, so a and d (medications) are out. Ice on impaired circulation causes vasoconstriction/injury. Guided imagery, relaxation breathing, and distraction reduce sympathetic activation. Multiple choice 131. Chart review for a 55-year-old with osteoarthritis intolerant of opioids: bed rest → increased

entries.h: 132. A client with actinic keratosis asks what it means for their health. How should the nurse respond?
entries.t: a. It's harmless and needs no treatment b. It's a cancer that spreads quickly and needs immediate surgery c. It's a chronic condition caused by sun exposure, and treatment can prevent it from becoming cancerous d. It's a cosmetic issue that can be removed if it bothers you Check c. Actinic keratosis is precancerous and can progress to squamous cell carcinoma; the nurse educates about cause and prevention without alarming or dismissing. Multiple choice

entries.h: 133. A client with plaque psoriasis makes which statement that indicates understanding of teaching?
entries.t: a. I should avoid sun exposure to prevent flare-ups b. I will apply a topical steroid daily c. I should gently remove scales after bathing while my skin is moist d. Once symptoms clear, I can stop medications Check c. Removing scales while moist lets topical steroids reach the plaque, not dead skin. Sun actually helps psoriasis; daily long-term steroid use should be avoided; it's a chronic condition. SATA

entries.h: 134. A nurse teaches a client with atopic dermatitis (eczema). Which interventions should be included? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Apply topical corticosteroids daily to affected areas during flare-ups b. Use moisturizers at least twice daily, especially after bathing c. Take daily bleach baths to prevent infection d. Use topical immunosuppressants for maintenance therapy e. Eliminate confirmed food allergens from the diet f. Take antihistamines as prescribed g. Avoid all sun exposure to prevent worsening symptoms h. Use wet-wrap therapy for severe flare-ups Check a, b, d, e, f, h. Steroids to flare areas, moisturize twice daily, immunosuppressant creams for maintenance, remove allergens, antihistamines, and wet wraps

entries.h: 135. During discharge planning after a total laryngectomy, which intervention should the nurse prioritize when collaborating with home health?
entries.t: a. Arrange weekly blood draws to monitor CBC b. Establish a schedule for wound and stoma management c. Schedule daily home radiation therapy d. Assign a home health aide to administer IV antibiotics Check b. The client is left with a stoma requiring ongoing management. The others are unnecessary/nonsensical (no chemo, no home radiation, no infection). SATA

entries.h: 136. A client newly diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea is taught about CPAP. Which statements should be included? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Use the CPAP every night and during naps b. It's okay to stop using CPAP when symptoms improve c. You may need to try different masks for comfort d. Clean the mask and tubing daily with mild soap and water e. Remove the mask if you wake during the night f. Regular CPAP use can reduce blood pressure and daytime fatigue Check a, c, d, f. CPAP is used whenever sleeping, mask fit varies, daily cleaning is needed, and consistent use lowers BP/fatigue. Symptoms recur if stopped; don't remove the mask mid-sleep. Multiple choice

entries.h: 137. A care plan for a client with chronic upper respiratory issues includes psychosocial interventions. Which most appropriately reflects understanding of psychosocial factors?
entries.t: a. Recommend social isolation to reduce exposure to triggers b. Promote smoking cessation through individualized behavioral counseling c. Encourage alcohol use to manage stress and improve sleep d. Advise limiting physical activity to avoid respiratory strain Check b. Psychosocial care supports the client's emotional/mental health; behavioral counseling addresses addiction. Isolation, alcohol, and limiting activity are harmful. Multiple choice

entries.h: 138. A client who had radiation for laryngeal cancer reports difficulty swallowing and decreased taste. Which intervention is most appropriate?
entries.t: a. Ensure the client has soft, moist foods in the plan of care b. Suggest commercial mouthwash several times a day c. Reassure the client symptoms will resolve within 1 week d. Limit oral hygiene to once daily to avoid irritation Check a. Soft, moist foods ease swallowing and enhance taste. Alcohol-based mouthwash is painful post-radiation; avoid definitive timeframes; oral hygiene should be frequent. Priority

entries.h: 139. A client has anterior epistaxis. Which is the priority action?
entries.t: a. Apply continuous pressure to the nares b. Instruct the client to blow their nose to clear clots c. Tilt the client's head back to stop the bleeding d. Place a warm compress on the nasal bridge Check a. Pinching the soft (cartilaginous) part of the nose for 10-15 minutes stops ~90% of anterior nosebleeds. Blowing dislodges clots; tilting back just redirects blood down the throat; the bridge is bone and can't be compressed. SATA

entries.h: 140. A nurse teaches about upper respiratory infections. Which are potential complications of a URI? (Select all that apply)
entries.t: a. Airway obstruction b. Epistaxis c. Meningitis d. Medicamentosa (rebound congestion) e. Aphonia (loss of voice) f. Pyelonephritis g. Sepsis h. Dysphagia Check a, b, c, d, e, g, h. Abscess/infection can obstruct the airway, spread to the brain (meningitis) or blood (sepsis), cause epistaxis, rebound congestion, laryngitis/aphonia, and dysphagia. Pyelonephritis is not a URI complication (strep can cause glomerulonephritis, not pyelonephritis). Priority

entries.h: 141. A nurse assesses four clients with pneumonia. Which should the nurse see first?
entries.t: a. 70-year-old with temp 101.5°F and chills b. 45-year-old with productive cough and fatigue c. 60-year-old who is confused with new-onset restlessness d. 30-year-old requesting pain med for lower back discomfort Check c. New-onset confusion/restlessness can signal hypoxemia-an ABC/neuro change. Fever, chills, cough, and fatigue are expected with pneumonia. Multiple choice

entries.h: 142. A client presents from home with fever, productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and crackles in the lower lobes. Which action promotes safety and infection control?
entries.t: a. Airborne isolation with N95 b. Droplet precautions; client wears a mask outside the room c. Limit fluid intake to reduce pulmonary congestion d.
